cert.title: Mobilithek — client certificate (PEM)
cert.description: PEM contents of the machine-account client certificate (mutual TLS). ONE certificate authenticates every Mobilithek feed — set it once, then just add each feed's subscription id. Recommended: generate your own keypair with `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -days 825 -keyout mobilithek.key.pem -out mobilithek.cert.pem -subj "/CN=openmapx-mobilithek"`, upload mobilithek.cert.pem under the machine account's 'Zertifikat hochladen' tab (no SMS needed), then paste mobilithek.cert.pem here and mobilithek.key.pem in the key field. Alternative: convert an issued .p12 with `openssl pkcs12 -in m.p12 -clcerts -nokeys | openssl x509` (cert) and `openssl pkcs12 -in m.p12 -nocerts -nodes | openssl rsa` (key).

steps: Register your organisation at mobilithek.info/registration-request; leave 'Organisation relevant gemäß MDV/PBefG' unchecked.
Subscribe to the offer(s) you want (each feed's offer IDs are listed in its subscription-id field).

Create a machine account at mobilithek.info/organisation/machine-accounts and upload your own certificate (generate it with the openssl command shown in this field's description, no SMS needed). Paste the certificate PEM here and its private key in the key field.
setup.notes: This ONE certificate authenticates every Mobilithek feed — set it once, then add each feed's subscription id. (The NRW state network is published under 'LVZ.NRW', not 'Straßen.NRW'.)

steps: Create a free account at 511on.ca/my511/register (or log in); an account is needed before a key can be requested.

api_key.title: 511NY data feed access (New York)
api_key.description: The access NYSDOT grants under the 511NY Developer Access Agreement, for the events and winter road conditions feeds (and the camera inventory).

setup.urlLabel: Read the 511NY data feed page and Developer Access Agreement
steps: Read the Developer Access Agreement on 511ny.org/help/24 (last updated 2026-09-18). Submitting a request accepts it.

Open the request form linked on that page ("CARS Agencies' XML Feed Request Form", shared by several state DOTs). Fill in Name, "Company, Agency, or Personal Use", the company or project name, and the email the approval should go to, and tick NY under the agencies.

Reason for Access is the only free-text field, so it must cover what the agreement asks a request to describe: the intended use and the product (name the traffic events, winter road conditions and camera inventory feeds); the intended market and the benefit to travelers; any similar products you have built or plan; and every intermediate or third-party disseminator. Name OpenConditions, the self-hosted data service that fetches the feeds for your map, and, if this instance serves its public API or federates with peers, those as recipients too. Then state that you accept the agreement and its attribution and display duties.

Ready-to-adapt reason: "I am requesting access to the NYSDOT (511NY) XML data feeds (traffic events, winter road conditions and the camera inventory) for OpenMapX, a free, non-commercial, open-source maps and navigation app. Our instance fetches the feeds through OpenConditions, our own self-hosted traffic data service, and shows live incidents, road work, closures, winter road conditions and traffic cameras on the map and in route planning, so travelers in New York can plan around them. Audience: the general public, free of charge. Similar products: none. Recipients: our app's end users through OpenConditions, operated by us; no other third parties, and we will tell NYSDOT before that changes. We will show when each report was published or last updated, keep the meaning of every report as NYSDOT published it, pass on NYSDOT's disclaimer, and credit 511NY / NYSDOT as the source. We accept the 511NY Developer Access Agreement."

Requests are reviewed weekly. An approval email brings the feed addresses, the access credential and the documentation. Send those to whoever maintains this OpenConditions instance: the feeds need their new addresses, and a reader if the format differs from the retired IBI 511 API, before they can be enabled.
setup.notes: Agreement duties: show when each report was published or last updated; keep the meaning of every report as published; use best efforts to pass on NYSDOT's disclaimer; keep NYSDOT informed of changes to your product, distribution plans and recipients. Permitted, not required: the "powered by 511NY" tag line with the unaltered 511NY logo and a link to 511ny.org; otherwise "511NY" may not be used to market or brand your product. Questions and feed problems go to the 511NY program manager named on 511ny.org/help/24. The old 511ny.org developer keys and API no longer work.

steps: Register at nap.si/en/registration (DARS / DRSI).

Request access and tick exactly the two DATEX II v3.3 datasets (under 'Other contents', XML, english): 'Traffic events (DATEX II v3.3)' and 'Roadworks (DATEX II v3.3)'. Leave everything else unticked.

Fill the Purpose/Description (min. 100 chars), set a Time period, agree to the terms, and submit. Ready-to-paste purpose: OpenMapX (https://openmapx.com) is a free, open-source maps and navigation app; we ingest the Traffic events and Roadworks DATEX II v3.3 datasets to display live road conditions and route around closures and roadworks in Slovenia, with CC-BY-SA attribution shown to users.
setup.notes: CC-BY-SA (ShareAlike). The B2B host (b2b.ncup.si) is credential-gated; the NAP account is sent as HTTP Basic — confirm the exact scheme when granted.
